culture: Many Mexican colonial towns have narrow cobblestone streets, so drivers sometimes fold in their mirrors
Cobblestone streets can flood when it rains
Skills and trades, like driving a taxi, often run in the family and are passed down from grandfather to grandson
A tianguis is a large open-air market in a town, often held on a specific day such as Tuesday
The Jardín is the central town garden or square, with trees and benches, and is the heart of social life
At night the Jardín fills with families, couples and mariachis
Mariachis play in the Jardín at night
Mariachis often play romantic songs, and couples sit on benches to listen
Polite formal address uses usted, as in "¿Necesita un taxi?" and "le llevo"
Common courteous phrases: "Buenas tardes, bienvenido", "suba, por favor", "Que disfrute", "Que le vaya bien", "Hasta la noche"
